verdicts.reason: A keeps the can on its teal circle and the headline wraps well. But the circle is clipped against the top edge, the tiny body copy is jammed against the top edge, and the three pills are scattered in a messy 2+1 cluster, with 'Summer Only' dropped alone under the CTA and almost touching the bottom. B pulls the teal circle away from the product and turns it into a logo disc behind GLACIER, so the can floats bare and tiny. Its headline breaks badly ('Mint is / back', with 'back' orphaned), and the body copy is squeezed into an illegible 6-line column of 1–2 words per line. B's stacked CTA and pills are tidier, but it loses more of the original's fidelity and typography.
